_comment: What was actually exercised before handoff. Do not mark true without doing it (docs/06). Everything marked true below was run against `next start` on the production build, in a real browser, not read off the source. The latest pass is the FIX-2 section 8 verification (see howEachWasChecked.fix2Verification2026-09-06): an independent QA pass over the four implementers' uncommitted FIX-2 work, run against a fresh `npm run build` and a fresh `next start` whose served asset hashes were confirmed against `.next` on disk before any testing began.

retired.heroDuotoneToColorMix: RETIRED, not failing and not fixed: the thing it measured no longer exists by design. FIX-2 section 1 removed the duotone treatment from the hero outright, so there is no longer a duotone-to-colour mix to verify. components/hero/heroShader.ts has no uMix, uDark or uLight uniform and no luminance step; the fragment shader now samples the texture, adds grain, and outputs. Confirmed at runtime, not only in source: WebGLRenderingContext.getUniformLocation was wrapped before any page script ran and every uniform the page set was recorded by name; the complete set on the hero canvas is uTexture, uCover, uPointer, uTime, uZoom, uGrain, uDisplace, plus three's own sprite uniforms (map, diffuse, opacity, center, rotation). The replacement assertion is heroFullColourAtPin0_50_100 below.

howEachWasChecked.fix2Verification2026-09-06: FIX-2 section 8 verification pass over the four implementers' uncommitted work on feat/next-redesign (HEAD bdda21b, changes in the working tree, hence the +fix2-worktree build tag). chrome-devtools and playwright MCP were unavailable this session, so everything was driven through puppeteer-core against system Chrome (headless, --use-gl=angle so WebGL is real), with pixels measured by sharp. Order, per CLAUDE.md's 'verify against the filesystem and the build output' rule: no node processes were running at the start (checked with tasklist); `npm run build` in web/ exited 0; `npx next start -p 3401` was started fresh AFTER that build; and before a single test ran, the served HTML's four CSS chunk hashes (4502c734eb4f2086, 59b390ce9c1e1ed0, 5b6875dfd53bfce1, bddfc0da8f438160) and the BUILD_ID (ETQVrazXFlYtkR5fXrcW1) were confirmed to match `.next/static/css` and `.next/BUILD_ID` on disk. Two of this pass's own measurement harnesses were found to be broken and were rebuilt before their results were believed; both are recorded in the relevant entries below rather than quietly fixed, because in each case the broken version produced a plausible-looking pass or fail.
howEachWasChecked.buildPasses: npm run build in web/, exit 0. Route / is 8.79 kB, 164 kB first load JS; /_not-found 994 B, 104 kB; shared 103 kB. No warnings.
howEachWasChecked.lintPasses: Carried from the prior pass; scripts/guardrails.sh, which `npm run lint` also runs, was re-run directly this pass. See guardrailsWebExitZero.
howEachWasChecked.typecheckPasses: Carried from the prior pass. `npx tsc` was run this pass only on components/whimsy/roomPuzzle.logic.ts in isolation, for the node logic check.
howEachWasChecked.guardrailsWebExitZero: `sh scripts/guardrails.sh` from web/: exit 0, no output. Confirmed it is not a silent no-op by reproducing its own file list (git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard minus node_modules/.next/public/scripts): 61 files, well over the script's own >=25 refusal threshold.
howEachWasChecked.guardrailsRootExitZero: `sh scripts/guardrails.sh` from the repository root: exit 0, no output. Same >=25-file refusal guard, same silence-means-pass contract.
howEachWasChecked.heroFullColourAtPin0_50_100: Real wheel events dispatched at the hero (Lenis ignores scrollTo), closing on each target from either side and then settling out the 0.6 scrub, so no frame was taken past the pin end. Progress was NOT inferred from scrollY: getUniformLocation was wrapped before page scripts ran, so uZoom was read straight off the GPU calls. Three stops, each landing exactly where intended: scrollY 0 with uZoom 1.0000 (progress 0), scrollY 674 with uZoom 1.2245 (which is 1 + 0.45 x smoothstep(0.5), i.e. progress 0.500), and scrollY 1345 with uZoom 1.4500 (progress 1, pin end at 1350). Mean green/red ratio over a 460x420 patch of photograph clear of the copy block: 0.890, 0.871, 0.888. Blue/red over the same patch: 0.898, 0.885, 0.914. Neutral at all three, no maroon suppression of green anywhere; for scale, the duotone bug this report used to carry measured 0.47. Screenshots hero-1440-0pct.png, hero-1440-50pct.png, hero-1440-100pct.png.
howEachWasChecked.heroZoomDrivenByScroll: Same three stops. uZoom read off the GPU goes 1.0000 -> 1.2245 -> 1.4500, which is exactly the 1.00 to 1.45 the brief specifies. Framing genuinely changes with it rather than the uniform moving alone: mean absolute pixel difference over the sampled photo patch is 44.8 (0 vs 50 percent), 49.3 (0 vs 100) and 42.5 (50 vs 100), and the three screenshots are visibly different crops of the same photograph.
howEachWasChecked.noGrayscaleOrMultiplyPhotoTreatment: Two ways. (1) Computed styles for every element on the page: no filter containing grayscale/sepia/saturate(0), no mix-blend-mode on any element that is or contains an img or canvas. The one blend on the site is app/globals.css .link::after, mix-blend-mode: multiply on the inline-link highlighter bar, which is over text and not over a photograph. The hero media container's computed background is rgb(255,255,255), per FIX-2 section 1. (2) A pixel sweep that cannot be fooled by the mechanism: every img on the page was scrolled into view, photographed and its mean chroma (max channel minus min channel) measured, then compared against the same file decoded independently from public/images. Rendered vs source: bootcamp-jeopardy 8.82 vs 7.36, ideathon-presenting 9.64 vs 9.61, summit-recruiter 44.51 vs 42.68, game-night-chess 51.28 vs 51.00. Every photograph renders at its file's own saturation. The two low-chroma images in the programs strip are low-chroma photographs, not tinted ones, which is exactly the confusion this cross-check exists to settle. HARNESS BUG WORTH RECORDING: the first run of this sweep reported four photographs as pure white, stdev 0. The cause was page.screenshot({clip}), whose rect in this Puppeteer is in PAGE coordinates while getBoundingClientRect returns VIEWPORT ones, so it photographed the wrong band of the document. Rebuilt to screenshot the viewport and cut with sharp.
howEachWasChecked.heroGlyphSpritesAreRealGlyphs: At 1440x900, both hero edge strips were photographed and the gold blobs cropped and magnified: hero-edge-left-1440.png, hero-edge-right-1440.png, hero-sprite-glyphs-zoom.png. All three glyphs are present and unmistakable as glyphs rather than polygons: a four-pointed sparkle (U+2726), a five-pointed star (U+2605) and an eight-spoked asterisk (U+2733) with visibly tapered spokes. Eight sprites were counted off the GPU (see below), and their world scales this run were 0.1022 to 0.1793, inside the brief's 0.08 to 0.18.
howEachWasChecked.heroGlyphSpritesRotate: Read, not inferred. The SpriteMaterial `rotation` uniform is written every frame by HeroScene's useFrame; with getUniformLocation wrapped, its value can be sampled directly. With the pointer parked at the centre of the viewport, all eight sprites' rotation uniforms advanced by exactly 0.203 rad over one second, against the brief's 0.2 rad/s. Independently, screenshots one second apart with the pointer parked differ at the sprite positions by mean-absolute-difference 5.3 to 10.7 against 2.9 for an equal-sized control patch of pure photograph, so the change is the sprites and not the film grain.
howEachWasChecked.heroGlyphSpritesScatterAndReturn: Sprite world positions read off the modelViewMatrix of each sprite draw (elements 12 and 13), so this is where the GPU put them, not where a screenshot suggested they were. Pointer parked at the centre, then moved to 0.35 world units inboard of a right-edge sprite, then back to the centre. Tracked sprite: x 1.7487 at rest, distance 0.349 from the pointer, well inside the 1.1-unit radius; pushed OUTWARD to x 2.1876 while the pointer was near; back to x 1.7487 exactly once it left. Its three right-hand neighbours moved the same way and returned to the same four x values they started on. y drifted downward by 0.511 over the roughly 5 seconds of the test, which is 0.10 units/s, inside the brief's 0.05 to 0.13 drift. HARNESS BUGS WORTH RECORDING, both of which produced a confident wrong answer first: (1) matching sprites between frames by nearest gold blob is ambiguous because they drift, and (2) the first attempt placed the pointer 0.35 units OUTBOARD of a right-edge sprite, which is past x = 1440, so no pointer event reached the canvas at all and every sprite sat still. That run would have read as a clean 'no scatter' failure. The rebuilt version keys sprites by their fixed per-sprite scale and refuses to run if the pointer lands off the canvas.
howEachWasChecked.heroGlyphSpritesRenderInGoldToken: FAILS, cosmetic. HeroScene.glyphTexture draws the glyphs with ctx.fillStyle = tokens.gold, which is #FFCC33 = rgb(255,204,51), but they reach the screen as rgb(255,154,8), a more saturated orange. Measured as the brightest 25 percent of gold pixels in one frame, with the nav's 'Join the List' pill in the SAME screenshot as the control: the DOM pill measures rgb(255,204,51) exactly, the sprite measures rgb(255,154,8). That is precisely the sRGB-to-linear transform of the token (0.8 -> 0.6038 -> 154, 0.2 -> 0.0331 -> 8), so a decode is being applied to the glyph texture that the renderer's LinearSRGBColorSpace output never encodes back. Suspects are the colour-space round trip between components/hero/HeroScene.tsx glyphTexture (texture.colorSpace = THREE.NoColorSpace, line ~115) and the Canvas onCreated (gl.outputColorSpace = THREE.LinearSRGBColorSpace, line ~253); the photo plane is unaffected because its ShaderMaterial samples with texture2D and does no colour work. Not fixed, per this pass's remit. Does not affect any FIX-2 section 8 assertion: the glyphs are the right glyphs, they rotate, and they scatter.
howEachWasChecked.missionRotatorOneLineAt1440: At 1440x900, measured off bounding boxes rather than looked at: prefix top -196.5, word top -204.2 (7.7px apart, same line), and the word's left edge 312 is past the prefix's right edge 298, so they are side by side and not wrapped. Container height is 84px, which is its own min-height, i.e. exactly one row. Container computed style matches FIX-2 section 5 line for line: display flex, flex-direction row, align-items center, flex-wrap wrap, gap 8px 14px, min-height 84px, padding-top 25px, margin-top 63px, border-top-width 1px. Prefix is Lora italic 23px in rgb(31,26,23); word is Archivo 800 at 39px with letter-spacing -1.365px, which is -0.035em at that size, in maroon rgb(122,0,25). At 390x844 it stacks under the prefix as the sub-640px rule requires (mission-390x844.png).
howEachWasChecked.missionRotatorGoldUnderline: Computed style on the word span: text-decoration-line underline, text-decoration-color rgb(255,204,51) which is the gold token exactly, text-decoration-thickness 5px, text-underline-offset 7px. All four as specified.
howEachWasChecked.missionRotatorRestsOnYouAndStops: Polled the word's textContent every 120ms for 16 seconds after scrolling it into view. Sequence observed, once, in order: 'Black students.' -> 'Latinx students.' (+1.87s, the first gap is short only because polling began mid-hold) -> 'first-generation students.' (+2.37s) -> 'you.' (+2.51s), reaching 'you.' 6.75s in. It then held 'you.' for the remaining 9.2s of that window, and a further 6 seconds of sampling at 250ms afterwards returned the single distinct value 'you.'. No loop, no fifth phrase, over 15 seconds of continuous observation after it settled.
howEachWasChecked.missionRotatorServerRestingState: curl of the freshly started production server, before any client JS: the raw HTML contains you.. The resting word the server draws is the final one, which is what CLAUDE.md rule 2 asks for. The same curl also carries all eight puzzle tiles in solved reading order (You / have / a / place / in / this / room / U+2733) as aria-labels, and the string 'duotone' appears zero times in the served HTML.
howEachWasChecked.navMark24pxBesideWordmark: The nav renders through next/image at a measured 24x24 CSS pixels, immediately left of the 'ColorStack UMN' wordmark span (mark right edge 96 vs wordmark left edge 104 at 1440; 44 vs 52 at 390). alt is empty, correctly, because the wrapping link carries aria-label 'ColorStack UMN, home'. Exactly one element on the whole page uses the mark: the footer and the mobile sheet carry the wordmark as text, as FIX-2 section 4 requires.
howEachWasChecked.navMarkIsGoldyGopher: KNOWN LIMITATION, recorded rather than reported as a bug. The file in the nav is the ColorStack stack mark, not the chapter mark with Goldy Gopher that FIX-2 section 4 asks for. public/images contains no Goldy file; the owner has been asked to supply one, which FIX-2 section 4 explicitly anticipates ('If the Goldy file isn't in public/images, tell me and I'll supply it'). Everything else about the slot, position, size and singleness, is built and verified, so dropping the file in is the whole remaining change.
howEachWasChecked.puzzleTwentyShufflesSolvable: In the shipped bundle, in the browser: clicked the real Shuffle button 20 times and after each read all nine slots back out of the DOM (the tile buttons' corner index spans, in grid order, with the non-button cell as the open space). All 20 boards had an even inversion count, which for a 3x3 is exactly the solvability condition, and all 20 were distinct. Move counter read 0 and the status line read the idle string after every shuffle.
howEachWasChecked.puzzleHintIsAlwaysALegalMove: After each of those 20 shuffles, clicked 'A little help' and located the hinted tile by its hint class, then checked LEGALITY, that the hinted slot is orthogonally adjacent to the open space, rather than checking that it lowers the Manhattan heuristic. 20 of 20 legal. The heuristic test the brief's section 8 sketch suggests would be wrong and was deliberately not used: an optimal move raises the Manhattan total a meaningful fraction of the time, measured at 70 of 434 moves, 16.1 percent, over the seeded node runs below. The implementer's note on this is correct.
howEachWasChecked.puzzleHintFollowedReachesSolved: Five fresh shuffles, each solved by clicking only what the hint pointed at: 19, 19, 23, 26 and 25 moves, every one finishing on 'You have a place in this room U+2733' read in grid order, with the container's data-solved attribute set, the status line reading "That's the whole sentence. You're in." and its data-tone reading solved. No page errors during any of it.
howEachWasChecked.puzzleStatusStringsAndMoveCounter: All three strings appear at their moments and nowhere else: after a shuffle, 'A place for every piece. Start with a tile beside the open space.'; after a hint, 'Try the highlighted tile.'; on solve, "That's the whole sentence. You're in." The counter reads 0 after Shuffle, 1 after one legal slide, and stays 1 after clicking a tile that is not adjacent to the open space, so it counts moves rather than clicks.
howEachWasChecked.puzzleLogicCompiledAndCheckedInNode: Independent of the browser, as the file is designed for. `npx tsc components/whimsy/roomPuzzle.logic.ts --strict --target ES2020 --module commonjs --lib ES2020 --types` exits 0 (the first attempt reported two errors from @types/three's GPUTexture, pulled in by the default ambient types and unrelated to this file; --types excludes them). Ran 20 shuffles driven by a seeded mulberry32 rather than Math.random, so the run is reproducible: 20 of 20 even inversion count, and 20 of 20 driven to the solved board by repeatedly applying nextSolutionMove, worst case 27 moves, every returned move legal. neighbors() spot-checked at the corners and centre: 0 -> [3,1], 4 -> [1,7,3,5], 8 -> [5,7].
howEachWasChecked.galleryCentredAt1440: window.__fcDebug was set through evaluateOnNewDocument, so it was true before the section ever mounted. window.__fcLayout after layout: centre {x: 0, y: 0}, count 12, cols 4, rows 3, viewport 2.827 x 2.651 world units. THAT NUMBER ALONE IS NOT A CHECK, and is not what this entry rests on: place() subtracts the bounding-box centre from every card before returning, and the debug hook then re-measures that same array, so centre is 0 by construction and cannot fail. So the cloud was measured again independently, from the modelViewMatrix of every card draw, which is where the GPU actually put them: bounding-box centre of the twelve drawn positions is x 0.0000, y 0.0131. Both inside the 0.05 the brief asks for; the residual y is the 0.02-amplitude bob.
howEachWasChecked.galleryCentredAt390: Reloaded at 390x844 with isMobile and hasTouch emulation and an iOS user agent. __fcLayout: centre {x: 0, y: 0}, count 8, cols 2, rows 4, viewport 1.570 x 2.651. Independent bounding-box centre off the drawn matrices: x 0.0000, y 0.0103. Both inside 0.05.
howEachWasChecked.galleryCardCounts12Desktop8Mobile: 12 cards drawn at 1440x900 and 8 at 390x844, counted two ways that agree: __fcLayout.count, and the number of distinct card matrices in one frame. The accessible button list carries all 12 photographs at both sizes, which is correct, since the mobile reduction is a rendering cost decision and not an access one.
howEachWasChecked.galleryEveryRenderedCardIsCandid: Network-level, so it reflects what was actually textured rather than what a prop claimed. Every /images/ request the page made was recorded: the desktop gallery fetched exactly 12 files, all under /images/candids/, and they are exactly the 12 entries carrying candid: true in content/landing.ts (ideathon-room, elevator-lobby, lab-typing, summit-couches, window-trio, staircase-landing, summit-duolingo, game-night-chess, lab-workstation, stairway-talk, summit-dining, red-chair). The mobile pass fetched the first 8 of the same list. The three photographs in that file WITHOUT candid: true (staircase-group, corridor-portrait, playful-boxing) were never requested at either viewport. The 12 accessible button labels match those 12 photographs' alt text, in file order.
howEachWasChecked.galleryHoverFacesCameraWithItalicCaption: Hovered a card by scanning a 9x9 grid of pointer positions across the canvas until the caption filled, then let the group's pointer tilt settle for 2 seconds before measuring. rotation.y read as atan2(m[8], m[10]) off each card's modelViewMatrix. The hovered card: 0.0000 rad of change over 1.2 seconds, i.e. stopped, and sitting -0.0138 rad (-0.79 degrees) from the nearest multiple of 2pi, i.e. square to the camera, the residual being the group's own 4-degree-max tilt. The other eleven cards moved 0.193 to 0.410 rad over the same 1.2 seconds, which is 0.16 to 0.34 rad/s against the brief's 0.15 to 0.35. On leaving, the same card resumed at 0.324 rad/s and the caption cleared. The caption itself: the hovered photograph's exact alt text, Lora, font-style italic, 14px, text-align left, its left edge at 92 flush with the canvas's left edge at 92, and its top at 1150.6 against the canvas bottom at 1126.6, so it is under the canvas and not over the card. Screenshot gallery-hover-facing-1440x900.png. NOTE ON THE FIRST ATTEMPT, which reported a hovered card 12 degrees off the front face and still turning: it matched cards between frames by world x, which the group's pointer tilt shifts by up to 0.07 units, and then fell back on scale as an identity key, which is useless here because the planes carry their size in the geometry and every card's matrix scale is exactly 1. Both are recorded because the broken version produced a plausible-looking failure.
howEachWasChecked.screenshotsBothViewports: hero, mission, gallery and puzzle at 1440x900 and at 390x844, eight files, plus the hero at 0/50/100 percent of the pin, the two hero edge strips, the magnified glyph triptych, the four sprite scatter frames and the hovered-gallery frame. All in the pass's scratch qa2/ directory, named for what they show.
howEachWasChecked.qaVerification2026-09-06: The prior pass, kept for provenance. Independent re-verification, chrome-devtools MCP against `npx next start`. First gotcha, recorded per CLAUDE.md's 'verify against the filesystem and the build output' rule: `next start -p 3200` was already running from a prior session BEFORE that pass's `npm run build`, so the browser was loading HTML that referenced CSS/JS chunk hashes from an OLD `.next` build while the files on disk were the NEW build's. Every check was re-run against a brand-new server with its served HTML's CSS hashes confirmed against disk first. The FIX-2 pass above repeated that discipline from scratch.
howEachWasChecked.heroCanvasGPU: Chromium via puppeteer with --use-gl=angle. <canvas> mounts inside the hero, WebGL context present, uniforms are being written every frame (they were read out of the GL calls for the hero checks above), frame loop runs.
howEachWasChecked.heroFallbackNoWebGL: n/a per owner direction 2026-09-06 (DESIGN.md v3.3 assumes WebGL; no-WebGL path is not a requirement). Not tested this pass.
howEachWasChecked.reducedMotionPath: n/a per owner direction 2026-09-06: no prefers-reduced-motion variant exists anywhere in this codebase, on purpose (DESIGN.md, "Motion is not optional"). Confirmed no matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion...)') read anywhere in web/components or web/app.
howEachWasChecked.guardrailsProvenToFail: Carried over from the implementer's pass (not re-run destructively this session): appending a literal hex to a CSS module and a real U+2014 to content/landing.ts both failed the script (exit 1), both reverted cleanly. This pass re-confirmed only that the script exits 0 on the untouched tree and is not silently scanning nothing.
howEachWasChecked.serverRenderedFinalState: Fresh curl of the newly started production server, 50938 bytes, parsed for content: hero photo and alt, hero lede, mission headline, the rotator resting on 'you.', the pull quote, both spec-sheet labels, the marginalia line, and all eight puzzle tiles in solved reading order, before any client JS runs.
howEachWasChecked.keyboardOnlyNavigation: Carried from the prior pass: Tab from the top through the brand link, all seven primary nav links and the nav Join pill with a visible gold 2px outline at every stop; Enter opens the gallery lightbox from a hidden a11y-list button, Escape closes it and returns focus to the trigger; arrow keys move focus within the puzzle grid; the mobile sheet opens, traps and returns focus.

Not asserted: isolating the lift needs a before-and-after comparison across a pointer move, and the same move changes the group's tilt, which moves every card in z by a comparable amount. It is not one of the section 8 checks. The hover behaviours section 8 does ask for, facing the camera and the caption, are both measured above.

knownGaps: Nav routes /about /programs /events /newsletter /opportunities /resources /wunderbar /contact /sponsor /privacy all 404. Landing only, as briefed. They appear as prefetch 404s in the console.
The nav mark is the ColorStack stack mark, not Goldy. FIX-2 section 4 anticipated this and asked to be told; public/images has no Goldy file. See howEachWasChecked.navMarkIsGoldyGopher.

Hero glyph sprites render as rgb(255,154,8) rather than the gold token rgb(255,204,51), a colour-space round trip, measured against the nav pill in the same frame. Cosmetic, unfixed, see howEachWasChecked.heroGlyphSpritesRenderInGoldToken.

The gallery canvas is 960px wide inside a 1320px section at 1440x900, because app/page.module.css roomLayout puts it in the left column of a two-column layout with the marginalia and glyph stickers in the right gutter. The cloud is correctly centred ON ITS CANVAS (measured pixel centre 552 against canvas centre 572), but the canvas is not the 'full container width' FIX-2 section 7 describes, so on screen the cloud sits left of the section's middle. Recorded as a layout decision for the owner to confirm, not scored: section 8's own gallery test is the bounding-box centre, which passes at both viewports.
components/ui/SideNav.tsx, components/editorial/MetaRow.tsx and MetaSidebar.tsx, and components/motion/ZoomImage.tsx are carried from the handoff and compile, but nothing on this page uses them.

public/images/colorstack-umn-mark-192.webp is 192px on its longest side and was KEPT despite the under-1200px deletion rule. It is the chapter mark, rendered at 24px in the nav, and the nav requires it.
RESOLVED and retired: the duotone-to-colour bug this report used to carry no longer applies. FIX-2 section 1 removed the duotone treatment entirely; see the retired block.
notes: No reduced-motion path exists and none is reported on: DESIGN.md, "Motion is not optional", owner-confirmed 2026-09-06 that no variant exists on purpose. One gradient exists on the whole site, the hero legibility scrim, authorised for contrast. The rose band carries ink text rather than white: white on #C6887F measures 2.9:1 and fails WCAG AA, ink measures 5.9:1 and passes; DESIGN.md-documented, owner-accepted. The FIX-2 section 8 pass found two things worth the owner's attention and neither is a broken feature: the nav mark is the stack mark rather than Goldy, which FIX-2 section 4 expected to be reported, and the hero glyph sprites render one colour-space transform away from the gold token. Everything else in section 8 passed, with the hero's zoom, the sprites' rotation and scatter, the gallery's centring and the hovered card's facing all measured off the GPU's own uniform and matrix writes rather than inferred from screenshots. Two of this pass's own harnesses produced confident wrong answers before they were rebuilt (a screenshot clip in the wrong coordinate space, and a pointer parked off the edge of the canvas); both are written up in place, because a check that cannot fail and a check that cannot pass are the same kind of mistake.
